task.description:
WF-03 Step 2 gate -- validate CODE-DESIGNER's design for ISS-0426 (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md). You are a HARD GATE: PASS or FAIL, and a FAIL routes back to CODE-DESIGNER for rework. Apply your own role's standard checks (every acceptance criterion covered, no implementation code, unambiguous enough to build from). This description names the run-specific points that most need your scrutiny -- it does not replace your checklist.

SCRUTINISE THESE SPECIFICALLY:

1. THE TEST-ONLY SEAM ON PRODUCTION CODE. The design adds a new `@doc false` test-only synchronous entry point to Letflow.Engine.Lua.Executor so Group 1 tests can call the private run_script/3 without going through Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/Task.yield. Adding production surface area purely to serve tests is a real design smell and needs to clear a bar. CODE-DESIGNER cites this file's OWN existing precedent: build_script_error/3 at executor.ex:449, a public-with-@doc-false function whose comment at line 438 justifies it via REQ-162 design section 4.2/AC3. ORCH has confirmed that precedent exists. YOUR job is to judge whether it genuinely LICENSES this new seam or is being stretched: read executor.ex:438-455 and REQ-162's design, and decide whether the new seam is the same KIND of thing. Consider explicitly whether a test-support module, a @compile-guarded definition, or simply making run_script/3 public-with-@doc-false would be cleaner, and whether the design's answer is reasoned or merely asserted.
   CRITICAL SUB-CHECK: does the seam BYPASS the wall-clock kill for the paths under test? If Group 1 tests no longer exercise the Task/timeout wrapper at all, confirm the design states what is thereby NO LONGER covered by those tests, and that something else still covers the wrapper. A restructure that silently deletes coverage of REQ-155's LUA-10 layer-2 kill would be a worse defect than the flake it fixes. ISS-0426's own scope note warns that option (b) 'moves the threshold without removing the sensitivity' -- the mirror-image risk here is removing the sensitivity by removing the test.

2. OPEN QUESTIONS LEFT TO ELIXIR-DEV. The design closes with OQ-1 (exact seam signature) and OQ-2 (whether the 2 max_heap_words-limited Group 1 sites need a different mechanism, since they route through run_with_heap_limit/5 rather than run_script/3). Your role's bar is 'unambiguous enough to build from'. Judge whether these are legitimate implementation latitude or whether OQ-2 in particular is an unresolved DESIGN question being passed downstream -- if the design does not know whether its own mechanism covers 2 of its 11 Group 1 sites, that is a design gap, not a build detail. Say which it is and FAIL if it is the latter.

3. THE ENUMERATION'S CORRECTNESS. CODE-DESIGNER reports finding ISSUE-FIXER's enumeration incomplete: 5 additional Group-1-shaped call sites in the REQ-154 instruction-budget block, and 2 tests (executor_test.exs:656 and :887) that are internally MIXED (one Group-1-shaped call and one genuinely-racing Group-2 call in the same test body). ISS-0426's acceptance criterion 1 requires the enumeration be explicit and complete, with each test's timing assumption stated. VERIFY THE ENUMERATION YOURSELF against test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs -- do not accept either agent's count. Report the count you independently derive. The mixed tests are the highest-risk item: confirm the design says exactly what happens to a test whose two halves need opposite treatments, and that the answer does not lose either half's coverage.

4. TAG WIRING (ISS-0426 AC5). The design adds @tag :lua_wallclock_race, excluded in test/test_helper.exs and run in a new isolated subprocess in lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex (a sibling to run_wasm_hang_tests/0). Verify the wiring genuinely mirrors the :wasm_hang shape in BOTH files and that a plain `mix test` and CI both stay correct. Check the deliberate choice NOT to reuse the :wasm_hang tag is sound (CODE-DESIGNER's stated reason: same family, different root cause). Confirm CI actually invokes mix letflow.check.test -- read .github/workflows/ci.yml -- because if CI runs plain `mix test` instead, the newly tagged Group 2 tests would be SILENTLY EXCLUDED FROM CI ENTIRELY and never run anywhere. That would be a BLOCKER.

5. HARD CONSTRAINT AC4. Confirm the design changes NO production timeout semantics: config/config.exs:17's 5_000 untouched, no production timeout constant raised or removed. This is REQ-155's LUA-10 security control.

6. CONCURRENT-RUN CONTENTION. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex is also owned by the live run WF03-ISS0418-20260902. Verify the design's change there is genuinely minimal and additive as claimed (one new sibling function, one new call site, zero existing lines touched) -- a claim ORCH will rely on when sequencing the merge. If it is not, say so, because ORCH's merge plan depends on it.

You may READ any file. Do not edit lib/ or test/ -- your step writes only its own handoff (and you may amend the design ONLY if your role's instructions permit it; otherwise FAIL back to CODE-DESIGNER). Complete the handoff with a clear PASS/FAIL, your independently derived enumeration count, and per-point verdicts. Commit it to branch feature/WF03-ISS0426-20260902.

result.summary:
HARD GATE: FAIL on point 2 (OQ-2 is a design gap, not implementation latitude). Design read in full (lib/letflow/design/iss426-wallclock-test-contention.md, 521 lines), plus the raw evidence: lib/letflow/engine/lua/executor.ex in full (execute_with_manifest/2,3, run_script/3, build_script_error/3 at :438-457, run_with_heap_limit/5 at :508-551, handle_yield_result/3), test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs in full (all 47 test declarations, all 44 execute_with_manifest call sites, all 31 timeout_ms literals independently grepped and read line-by-line), test/test_helper.exs, lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex (pre-edit, current content), mix.exs's aliases block, .github/workflows/ci.yml, config/config.exs:17, config/test.exs:180-195, and both prior handoffs (ISSUE-FIXER step-01, CODE-DESIGNER step-02).

PER-POINT VERDICTS:

1. TEST-ONLY SEAM -- PASSES with a minor gap, not independently fatal. build_script_error/3's precedent (executor.ex:438-457, verified by direct read) is real and accurately cited: a @doc false public function, in-file comment explicitly justifying it as 'the shaping-function level test seam' for bypassing an outer mechanism that isn't the thing under test -- genuinely the same KIND of justification the new seam claims. CRITICAL SUB-CHECK ANSWERED CORRECTLY: the design does NOT silently lose LUA-10 coverage. Independently verified against my own full-file read: none of the 11 Group-1 tests assert wallclock_timeout, and Group 2's 11 tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed) keep every existing assertion/workload/timeout value unchanged, still racing a real Task.yield or run_with_heap_limit/5 timeout -- REQ-155's LUA-10 kill stays fully exercised. GAP: the design does not explicitly weigh the two alternatives the handoff named (a separate test-support module; simply making run_script/3 public-with-@doc-false instead of adding a new wrapper) against 2.1.1-A -- it only compares 2.1.1-A against 'raise the timeout instead' (a different axis: whether to remove the race at all, not where the seam should live). Recorded as a should-fix, not independently gate-failing.

2. OPEN QUESTIONS -- FAIL. OQ-1 (exact seam name/arity) is legitimate implementation latitude -- behavior, precedent, and constraints (a)/(b)/(c) are all pinned; naming is a real 'guessing at ergonomics' question, not a design gap. OQ-2 is NOT legitimate latitude -- it is an unresolved design question. Independently read run_with_heap_limit/5 (executor.ex:508-551): it contains its OWN bounded receive/after clause -- `after timeout_ms -> Process.exit(pid, :kill) ... {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, timeout_ms}}` -- structurally the identical wall-clock-race shape Task.yield has, just hand-rolled via :erlang.spawn_opt/2 instead of Task.Supervisor. OQ-1's proposed seam only bypasses Task.yield on the nil-heap-words path; it does nothing for the 2 heap-limited Group-1 sites (REQ-156 AC-1 at line 605, AC-2 at line 644) or the 2 mixed tests' heap-limited memory_result arms (line 672, line 910) -- all four/five of these call sites would still race through run_with_heap_limit/5's own after-clause exactly as today, meaning ISS-0426's filed failure MODE (a fast, non-racing-in-principle test occasionally observing wallclock_timeout under contention) remains structurally possible for these sites even after the fix ships. The design's own §2.1 table lists these rows as ordinary Group-1 entries with no inline flag; only §7's OQ-2 admits 'the concrete mechanism may need to be... left for ELIXIR-DEV to resolve during implementation.' Per the handoff's own stated bar, this is exactly a case where 'the design does not know whether its own mechanism covers 2 of its 11 Group 1 sites' -- a design gap, not a build detail.

3. ENUMERATION -- substantively correct; INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED COUNT: 11 distinct Group-1 tests, 11 distinct Group-2-tagged tests (9 pure + 2 mixed), 22 distinct tests total, matching the design's own §2.1/§2.2 table CONTENTS (11 rows each) despite the design's own prose header at §2.1 claiming '15 call sites across 10 tests' -- arithmetically wrong against its own table (correct arithmetic from the table itself: 11 rows collapsing from 11 distinct test-declaration lines, since 2 of those 11 tests each contribute 2 timeout_ms call sites -- 14 call sites total, not 15; 11 tests, not 10). Independently verified test-by-test against the raw file (all 47 `test "..." do` declarations grepped, all 31 timeout_ms literals grepped and read in context) -- no test omitted or miscounted in the design's actual table data, only its own summary sentence undercounts by one test. The mixed tests (656, 887) are confirmed correct in substance: each contains one Group-2-shaped racing arm (timeout_result, timeout_ms: 200 at lines 665/903) and two Group-1-shaped arms (budget_result nil-heap at 658/896, plus a THIRD arm not flagged as a separate category by the design's prose -- memory_result at 672/910, which is Group-1-shaped in its ASSERTED OUTCOME but heap-limited in MECHANISM, i.e. it is simultaneously a mixed-test arm and an OQ-2-affected call site). Neither arm's coverage is lost: §2.4 keeps all three arms' assertions/workload unchanged and tags the whole test into Group 2, so the racing arm keeps racing and the two non-racing arms keep asserting what they always did -- this part of the design is sound. The undercount in §2.1's header is a documentation-accuracy defect worth a rework note but not independently gate-failing; it compounds with point 2's finding since 5 of the 14 Group-1 call sites (605 x2, 644 x1, 672, 910) are heap-limited and OQ-2-uncovered.

4. CI TAG WIRING -- PASS, verified with direct quotes. .github/workflows/ci.yml:126 `run: mix letflow.check`. mix.exs's aliases block (verified lines 91-108): `"letflow.check": ["letflow.check_toolchain", "letflow.check_requirements_registration", ..., "letflow.check_deferral_staleness", ..., "letflow.check.test"]` -- letflow.check.test is the alias's final step, so CI genuinely invokes it, not a plain `mix test`. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex (current/pre-edit content read in full) already calls run_wasm_hang_tests() from run/1's success branch; the design's proposed run_lua_wallclock_race_tests() sibling call would run through the exact same chain CI already exercises for :wasm_hang -- no silent-exclusion risk. Deliberate non-reuse of the :wasm_hang tag name is sound: ISSUE-FIXER's registry lookup (step-01, verified) established same-family-not-same-root-cause (no shared native thread pool on the Lua side, no permanently-leaking resource), so a shared tag would misleadingly imply a shared remediation mechanism.

5. AC4 HARD CONSTRAINT -- PASS, verified. config/config.exs:17 reads `config :letflow, lua_wallclock_timeout_ms: 5_000` (unchanged); confirmed via `git diff main...HEAD --stat` that config/config.exs does not appear in this branch's diff at all -- not merely unedited by the design's text, structurally absent from the change set.

6. CONCURRENT-RUN CONTENTION -- PASS. lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex is not yet modified on this branch (absent from `git diff main...HEAD --stat`, confirming Step 2 made no code edits, consistent with a design-only step). The design's described change (one new private function mirroring run_wasm_hang_tests/0's shape verbatim with 3 substitutions, one new call site in run/1's success branch, zero existing lines of run_wasm_hang_tests/0/stream_and_capture/2/collect/2 touched) is genuinely minimal and additive as claimed, verified against the actual current file content (read in full) -- ORCH's merge-sequencing plan against WF03-ISS0418-20260902 can rely on this claim.

OVERALL: FAIL, per core-directives.md's 'FAIL immediately on any single failed check -- no partial credit' and this handoff's own explicit instruction to FAIL if OQ-2 is a design gap rather than build latitude. Routing back to CODE-DESIGNER with the specific, actionable fix required.

issues.description: Point 2 -- OQ-2 is an unresolved design question, not legitimate implementation latitude. run_with_heap_limit/5 (executor.ex:508-551, independently read) contains its own bounded receive/after timeout_ms clause producing {:error, {:wallclock_timeout, timeout_ms}} -- the identical race shape Task.yield has. OQ-1's seam only bypasses Task.yield on the nil-heap-words path and does nothing for the 2 heap-limited Group-1 tests (REQ-156 AC-1 line 605, AC-2 line 644) plus 2 heap-limited arms inside the mixed tests (memory_result at line 672 and line 910) -- 5 call sites across 4 tests remain exposed to ISS-0426's exact failure mode after this design ships. REQUIRED FIX: the design must specify a concrete synchronous (or otherwise race-free) mechanism for the max_heap_words-limited path -- e.g. a second @doc false seam that calls the process-spawn-and-receive body of run_with_heap_limit/5 without its own after-clause, mirroring 2.1.1-A's reasoning for the nil case -- and add it to the design's own hard-constraint/coverage tables (§2.1, §3) rather than leaving it as an open question. If a race-free mechanism is not feasible for the heap-limited path, the design must say so explicitly and either (a) argue why the residual race is acceptably improbable with a same rigor as the diagnosis's negative-reproduction evidence, or (b) route those 4-5 sites into Group 2's tag-and-isolate treatment instead, updating §2.1/§2.2's tables and counts accordingly.

Point 3 -- §2.1's own prose header ('15 call sites across 10 tests') is arithmetically inconsistent with its own table, which lists 11 rows spanning 11 distinct test-declaration lines (253, 273, 283, 299, 448, 605, 644, 812, 861, 983, 1052) and 14 total timeout_ms call sites (2 of the 11 tests -- 253/AC-1 and 861/AC4 -- each contribute 2 rows). Independently re-derived by grepping and reading all 47 test declarations and all 31 timeout_ms literals in test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs: the table's DATA is correct; only the summary sentence undercounts. Fix the header to '14 call sites across 11 tests' when reworking for point 2, since the OQ-2 fix will likely touch this same table.

Point 1 -- the design does not explicitly weigh a test-support module or a plain public-with-@doc-false run_script/3 against the new-wrapper-function shape of 2.1.1-A, though the handoff asked for that comparison by name. The eventual choice may well remain 2.1.1-A (it is well precedented), but the design should record the comparison rather than only comparing against 'raise the timeout instead,' which is a different axis (whether to race at all, not where the seam lives).

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: resolve OQ-2 as a concrete design element (not an open question) covering the 4-5 heap-limited Group-1-shaped call sites (executor_test.exs lines 605, 644, and the mixed tests' memory_result arms at 672/910), correct §2.1's 'call sites/tests' arithmetic to match its own table, and add the test-support-module/public-run_script/3 alternatives comparison for the seam. Resubmit to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR.
